findings.issue_summary: User-Initiated Collection: Email data is sent via the backend email-service when the user explicitly triggers email sending. Disclosure exempt per Case 3, but EMAILS must be declared in the Play Store Data Safety form.
findings.evidence: email-service/src/emailService.js lines 37-49: The enviarEmail function sends email data (subject line 'assunto', HTML body 'corpoHtml', recipient 'destinatario', sender name 'remetenteNome', PDF attachment) via Gmail SMTP. Routes defined in routes.js line 70-104 expose POST /enviar accepting userId, destinatario, assunto, corpoHtml, pdfBase64, pdfNome, remetenteNome — all transmitted to the developer's backend and then to Gmail. The user explicitly triggers this action (user fills form and clicks send).
findings.recommendation: Declare EMAILS data collection in the Play Store Data Safety section under 'App functionality'. Since the user initiates the email sending (Case 3), prominent in-app disclosure is exempt, but the data type must be listed in the store listing's Data Safety form.

findings.issue_summary: Data Safety Compliant (Local-Only): No off-device transmission of device ID data detected. The getUniqueId pattern referenced in the data sources resolves to a minification artifact (SVG path parser code), not actual device ID collection. No IMEI, advertising ID, Firebase installation ID, or other device identifier collection was found in the source code.
findings.evidence: The getUniqueId string appears in dist/assets/index.es-BQdJycl1.js line 5 within SVG path parsing context (ARC commands, path data). grep of all source directories (src/, android/app/src/main/java/) for getUniqueId, deviceId, advertisingId, advertising_id returned no results indicating actual device ID collection. The Android manifest includes the AD_ID permission but no Ads SDK or analytics SDK that would use it is integrated in the build dependencies.
findings.recommendation: No action required. Verify in the Play Store Data Safety form that DEVICE_ID is not inadvertently declared. The AD_ID permission in manifest may be auto-included by Google Play Services and does not indicate active collection without a corresponding SDK.

findings.issue_summary: Data Safety Compliant (Local-Only): No off-device transmission of date of birth or similar personal info detected. The dob pattern referenced in the data sources is a minification artifact within React/Dexie/PDF vendor bundle code. No actual date of birth collection or transmission was found in the source code.
findings.evidence: The dob string appears in dist/assets/index-PqeuXPtB.js within minified vendor library code (React/Dexie/Supabase bundle). grep of all source directories for dob, birth, nascimento, dataNasc returned no results related to date of birth collection or transmission. The one match in translationService.ts line 137 is a currency code 'NIO' (Cordoba Oro), unrelated to date of birth.
findings.recommendation: No action required. Verify in the Play Store Data Safety form that PERSONAL_INFO_OTHER is not inadvertently declared.
